Few roles appeal to me more than logistics because they turn planning, problem-solving, and service into real-world impact every day. I am from Germany, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 500. What first drew me in was the satisfaction of seeing how order can keep people, products, and businesses connected. That connection became especially real on a family road trip when we unexpectedly passed one of the regional warehouses I help support, and my family insisted we stop so I could show them “where all the planning happens.” Seeing them connect my behind-the-scenes work to the products arriving in stores made the profession feel even more meaningful. It is this perspective that has shaped my ambition to build a career as a Logistics Coordinator, where I can combine structured planning with day-to-day operational responsibility.

My academic background and project work have strengthened that direction, including completing 5 projects with tangible outcomes. In one role, I had to use a method that was completely new to me; within a few weeks I was applying it confidently, and soon after I was the person colleagues came to when they needed someone to walk them through it. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value those moments because they reflect the importance of clear communication and dependable coordination.

I have also seen how logistics depends on steady follow-through. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when deadlines and revisions demanded it so that progress continued. I am now eager to bring this combination of structured thinking, practical follow-through, and genuine enthusiasm for keeping operations running smoothly to a Logistics Coordinator role.

Originally from Brazil, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and across my work I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes. In particular, I have built my understanding of web development through steady, practical experience. In one role, I needed to use a new technique that the work required; within a couple of months I had learned it well enough to apply it independently in my own tasks. On another project, a recurring issue was slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on, and I value those moments because they reflect the collaborative side of development.

During one extended period of delivery, I also identified a substantial piece of work that sat outside my formal responsibilities, began it on my own initiative, and carried it through over many months until it was completed. Altogether, these experiences have prepared me to contribute as a Web Developer with a clear sense of purpose, steady follow-through, and a genuine commitment to building reliable, engaging digital experiences.

These experiences have strengthened my commitment to physiotherapy and my ability to translate clinical assessment into tailored, achievable rehabilitation plans that patients can realistically follow.
